title: Starting Price of a Protected Substitute under the Contract Pricing Agreement
content:
## Starting price of a protected substitute — Contract Pricing Agreement

The protected price of a substitute for a discontinued Contract Pricing Agreement contract item is set against the ending price — the contract unit price that ends on the discontinued item's close-out line — and the substitute's unit price on its latest regular shipment, as the regular shipment lines of the substitute on the customer's Ship-To Fulfillment Account records show it (backorder fills are not regular shipments).

| Substitute's unit price on its latest regular shipment | Protected price |
|---|---|
| Below the ending price | The substitute's own unit price |
| 15 percent or more above the ending price | The ending price plus the product of 0.1 and the difference between the two |
| From the ending price up to less than 15 percent above it, or no regular shipment | The ending price |

**Cases (hypothetical ending price 10.0000).** Substitute at 9.5000: protected price 9.5000. Substitute at 12.0000 (20 percent above): 10.0000 plus 0.1 times 2.0000, which is 10.2000. Substitute at 11.4000 (14 percent above): 10.0000. Substitute with no regular shipment yet: 10.0000.
